program.name: Temporary Assistance (TANF)
program.description:
Temporary Assistance gives monthly cash help to Missouri families with children. You can get your cash benefit on an EBT card or by direct deposit.

Most adults must take part in Missouri Work Assistance to get job training and help finding work.

Your final benefit may be different from this estimate. Family Support Division may count income from some adults in your home even if they are not part of your case. Special rules also apply when someone in the household receives SSI. Temporary Assistance also has a limit on savings and other resources, and this estimate may not reflect it. You can usually get Temporary Assistance for up to 45 months. If you got TANF before, you may have less time left. Some people may qualify for more time.

To apply, select Apply Now. First, watch the orientation video. Then complete and send the application and required forms to Family Support Division.

documents.text: Proof of identity (e.g., driver's license, state ID, passport)
Proof of the child's age or relationship to you (e.g., birth certificate or guardianship papers)
Social Security Number or proof you applied for one, if required
Proof of Missouri residency, if requested (e.g., utility bill, lease agreement)
Proof of self-employment income (e.g., tax return, business ledgers or receipts)
Proof of qualified immigration status, if required (e.g., green card)
Proof of resources, if applicable (e.g., bank statements or property records)
School enrollment letter for household members age 17 or older who are in high school
Child care cost proof, if applicable (e.g., provider letter showing the prior month's cost)
Proof of registration or sign-in at jobs.mo.gov, if required
Signed Personal Responsibility Plan for your work or training activities
Child support forms, if a child's other living parent does not live with you
